name: FHIR R4
description: Any HL7 FHIR R4 server: search and read Patients, Observations, Conditions, Encounters, MedicationRequests, DiagnosticReports and any other resource type, plus the server's own capability statement. Bearer-token auth.
instructions:
**This is a generic FHIR R4 client, not a vendor connector.** Point it at any R4 server — a hospital's HAPI instance, a national test server, a vendor's sandbox — and it speaks the standard.
1. Set `FHIR_BASE_URL` to the server's base, the URL that answers `/metadata`. No trailing slash.
2. Set `FHIR_ACCESS_TOKEN` to a bearer token. Most real deployments use SMART on FHIR, whose authorisation flow issues short-lived tokens; obtain one and paste it here, or use a long-lived service token if the server offers one. A server that needs no auth still needs a placeholder here — put anything.

**Start with `fhir_get_capability_statement`.** FHIR servers differ enormously in which resource types they hold and which search parameters they support, and `/metadata` is the machine-readable answer. Guessing produces a lot of confident 400s.

**Search parameters are per resource type**, and modifiers matter: `name:contains=smith`, `birthdate=ge1980-01-01`, `code=http://loinc.org|85354-9`, `_lastUpdated=gt2026-09-01`. Prefixes on numbers and dates are `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `lt`, `ge`, `le`. A token search takes `system|code`, and the pipe is significant.

**Results are a Bundle.** The rows live in `entry[].resource`, the count in `total` (which some servers omit), and paging in `link[]` with `relation: "next"` — follow that URL rather than computing an offset. `_count` requests a page size; servers are free to ignore it.

**`_include` and `_revinclude` fetch related resources in the same Bundle**: `_include=Observation:patient` brings each observation's Patient along.

**This is patient data.** Anything read here is almost certainly health information under GDPR Article 9 or HIPAA. Whether an LLM may see it is a question about your legal basis and your processor agreements, not about this connector — decide it before installing, not after.

**Read-only by design**: no create, no update, no delete. A clinical record is not a thing an agent should write into by accident.

tools.name: fhir_get_capability_statement
tools.description: Read the server's CapabilityStatement: which resource types it holds, which interactions and search parameters each supports, and its FHIR version. Start here — servers differ enormously.

tools.name: fhir_search
tools.description: Search any resource type with FHIR's standard parameters. The general-purpose tool — the capability statement tells you which parameters this particular server supports.

resourceType.description: FHIR resource type, e.g. Patient, Observation, Condition, Encounter, MedicationRequest.

query.description: Search parameters as a query-string fragment, e.g. `name:contains=smith&birthdate=ge1980-01-01`.

count.description: Requested page size (_count). Servers may ignore it.

sort.description: Sort parameter (_sort), e.g. -date for newest first.

include.description: Related resources to pull into the Bundle (_include), e.g. Observation:patient.

tools.name: fhir_read_resource
tools.description: Read one resource instance by type and id, returning the full resource rather than a Bundle entry.

id.description: Resource logical id, as it appeared in a Bundle entry.

tools.name: fhir_search_patients
tools.description: Search Patients by name, identifier, birth date or family name. Modifiers matter: `name:contains` for a partial match, `ge`/`le` prefixes on dates.

name.description: Name search across given and family names.

birthdate.description: Birth date with an optional prefix, e.g. 1980-01-01 or ge1980-01-01.

tools.name: fhir_get_patient_observations
tools.description: Read the Observations recorded for one patient — vital signs, laboratory results, measurements — optionally narrowed to one LOINC code or category.

category.description: Observation category, e.g. vital-signs, laboratory, imaging.

date.description: Effective date with an optional prefix, e.g. ge2026-01-01.

tools.name: fhir_get_patient_conditions
tools.description: Read the Conditions recorded for one patient — the problem list — with their clinical and verification status.

clinical_status.description: Clinical status, e.g. active, recurrence, resolved.

tools.name: fhir_get_patient_encounters
tools.description: Read the Encounters for one patient — admissions, visits and consultations — with their class, period and the practitioners involved.

status.description: Encounter status, e.g. finished, in-progress, planned.

date.description: Encounter period with an optional prefix, e.g. ge2026-01-01.

tools.name: fhir_get_patient_medications
tools.description: Read the MedicationRequests for one patient — what has been prescribed, in what dosage, by whom and with what status.

status.description: Request status, e.g. active, completed, stopped, on-hold.

tools.name: fhir_get_patient_reports
tools.description: Read the DiagnosticReports for one patient — laboratory panels, imaging reports and pathology — with their category, status and conclusions.

date.description: Report date with an optional prefix, e.g. ge2026-01-01.

tools.name: fhir_get_patient_everything
tools.description: Run the $everything operation on one patient: every resource the server associates with them, in one Bundle. Powerful, large, and not supported by every server.

since.description: Only resources changed after this instant (_since), ISO 8601.
